title: Auto Layout essentials
summary: Auto Layout positions views using rules (constraints) like "20pt from the left" instead of fixed frames, so the UI adapts to any screen size, rotation and text size.
body: **In simple words:** You describe relationships: "this label is 16pt below the image and as wide as the screen minus margins". The layout engine solves these equations and computes every frame.

**Enough constraints:** each view needs enough rules to know its x, y, width and height. Too few = ambiguous layout (view jumps or is missing). Conflicting = "Unable to simultaneously satisfy constraints" in the console and one rule is broken.
**Intrinsic content size:** labels, buttons and image views know their natural size from content, so you often need only position constraints.

**Hugging vs compression resistance:** **Content hugging** = "I do not want to grow bigger than my content" (high = stays small). **Compression resistance** = "I do not want to shrink smaller than my content" (high = text will not be truncated). Used when two labels compete for space in a row.
**Priorities:** 1000 is required; lower priorities are "nice to have" and can break gracefully.

**Tools:** anchors in code (`label.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo:...)`), `UIStackView` to remove most manual constraints, and `translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false` for views made in code.
**Self-sizing cells:** constraints from the cell's content top to bottom let table/collection cells size themselves to their content.
keyPoints: Constraints describe relationships; the engine computes frames.
Each view needs unambiguous x, y, width, height.
Hugging = resist growing; compression resistance = resist shrinking.
UIStackView for most linear layouts; activate constraints in batches with `NSLayoutConstraint.activate`.

code.caption: Constraints in code

mistakes: Adding constraints repeatedly in `viewDidLayoutSubviews` or `updateConstraints` without removing old ones.
Mixing manual frame setting with Auto Layout on the same view.
followups: **How do you debug a broken layout?** Read the console log, use the View Debugger, give constraints identifiers, check for ambiguity with `hasAmbiguousLayout`.
**How do you animate a constraint change?** Change the `constant`, then call `view.layoutIfNeeded()` inside `UIView.animate`.
**Frames vs Auto Layout performance?** Manual frames can be faster for very complex cells, but Auto Layout is fine for most screens.
